# Opal Pettigrew

## Overview

- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028)</sub>
- **Status:** deceased  <sub>[v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)</sub>
- **Origin:** Brierley  <sub>[v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)</sub>
- **Role:** schoolteacher  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)</sub>

## Appearance

Opal is considered extraordinarily beautiful, possessing a striking physical presence with radiant skin, a full figure, and big, vivid blue eyes. In her youth, she wore a long blonde plait, and as a young woman she styled her blonde hair with flowers such as red geraniums. Before her death, her bout with galloping consumption left her extremely slender, with pale, fragile hands and a feverish flush on her cheeks.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P28](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0028), [v1 c30 P43](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0043), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c11 P4](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0004), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006)_

## Personality

Opal was lively, sunny, and quick to laugh, enjoying the pleasant aspects of life and displaying a sentimental tone in her writings. She was deeply preoccupied with male attention, suitors, and romance, often indulging in talk about her admirers. In crises or moments of panic, she was prone to hysterics and weeping. Facing her terminal illness, she struggled with fear and homesickness regarding the unfamiliarity of the afterlife.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P39](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0039), [v1 c23 P16](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0016), [v1 c26 P6](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0006), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c28 P36](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0036), [v1 c35 P1](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0001), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c5 P7](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0007), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P37](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0037)_

## History

Opal grew up in Brierley among several older sisters. As a student at Brierley school, she belonged to a writing group called the Story Club with her classmates and often spent time playing near the pond with friends like Nell Harcourt, Isolde Pembroke, and Odette Pullen. After qualifying at Regent's Academy as the most beautiful student of her cohort, she took up a teaching job at the local school in Delford. Over the years, she entertained numerous suitors, receiving proposals from figures such as Nelson Atkins and the Tullyvale schoolmaster, though she turned them down. In her final year, she suffered a severe bout of chest congestion during the winter while visiting Boston in the autumn prior, which developed into terminal galloping consumption. Although she planned to teach at Pale Sands in the fall, her health rapidly declined. Before her death, she reconciled with her childhood friend Em White and shared her anxieties about dying with Nell Harcourt. She passed away quietly in her sleep during the summer and was buried in Brierley.

_Sources: [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v1 c28 P7](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0007), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060), [v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056), [v3 c8 P3](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0003), [v3 c11 P6](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0006), [v3 c11 P34](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0034), [v3 c11 P53](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0053), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010), [v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013), [v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015), [v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023), [v3 c14 P30](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0030)_

## Background by volume

- grew up in Brierley in a family with numerous older sisters who married quickly  <sub>[v1 c18 P15](../source/v01-c18.md#nw-v01-c18-p0015), [v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>
- had her warts cured using an enchanted stone given by Mary Joe  <sub>[v1 c16 P18](../source/v01-c16.md#nw-v01-c16-p0018)</sub>
- was hidden in a pantry when her sister Tabitha received a marriage proposal  <sub>[v1 c26 P17](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0017)</sub>
- attended Brierley school and was a member of the Story Club  <sub>[v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c26 P21](../source/v01-c26.md#nw-v01-c26-p0021), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010)</sub>
- attended Regent's Academy and won recognition as its most beautiful student  <sub>[v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006)</sub>
- secured a teaching position at Delford school  <sub>[v2 c19 P59](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0059), [v2 c19 P60](../source/v02-c19.md#nw-v02-c19-p0060)</sub>
- rejected a marriage proposal from Nelson Atkins after discovering it was copied from an etiquette book  <sub>[v2 c26 P56](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0056)</sub>
- visited Boston during the autumn  <sub>[v3 c11 P34](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0034)</sub>

## Quotes

> Neither do I. Floating downward does not bother me when two or three of us are occupying the flat and we are able to sit upright. During those times, it is enjoyable. However, lying flat and acting as if I were deceased—that is something I simply could not do. Fear would actually kill me.  <sub>[v1 c28 P1](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0001)</sub>

> Oh, she appears truly deceased. It fills me with fear, girls. Is it really proper for us to perform in this manner, do you think? Mrs. Sowerby claims that any drama-acting is dreadfully sinful.  <sub>[v1 c28 P13](../source/v01-c28.md#nw-v01-c28-p0013)</sub>

> Because—because—oh, Nell, I am not scared that I will fail to get into heaven. I belong to the church. But—everything there is going to be so unfamiliar. I ponder—and ponder—and it makes me so scared—and—and—homesick. Of course, heaven has to be extremely beautiful, as the Bible states—however, Nell, it will not be like what I am accustomed to.  <sub>[v3 c14 P13](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0013)</sub>

> I can’t help it. Even if what you say about heaven is true—and you can’t be sure—it may be only that imagination of yours—it won’t be just the same. It can’t be. I want to go on living here. I’m so young, Nell. I haven’t had my life. I’ve fought so hard to live—and it isn’t any use—I have to die—and leave everything I care for.  <sub>[v3 c14 P15](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0015)</sub>

> It—it will not take much time now, Nell. I am certain of that. And I would prefer to have you over anybody else. Of all the girls I attended school alongside, I always favored you the most. You never showed jealousy, or malice, as a few of them did. Poor Em White came by to visit me yesterday. Do you recall that Em and I were great friends for three years while attending school? And subsequently we fell out at the time of the school concert. Ever since, we have not uttered a word to one another. Was it not foolish? Any occurrence of that sort appears foolish at present. However, Em and I resolved the former dispute yesterday. She mentioned that she would have conversed years back, except she believed I would refuse to. And I refrained from ever conversing with her since I was convinced she would refuse to converse with me. Is it not peculiar the way folks misjudge one another, Nell?  <sub>[v3 c14 P23](../source/v03-c14.md#nw-v03-c14-p0023)</sub>
